guard: a leading --json, -j or --plain before a command that takes its words raw is a usage error, never one of its words
why: The leading output flags move after the command word to be read as the command's own flags. A command that takes its words raw parses none, so the move handed them to it as words: cotal --json __complete status completed a line whose command word was --json.
The suite runs the built binary, so the mutation rebuilds in afterRestore.

mutations.name: leading output flags move after a raw-word command
mutations.find:
if (output.length && takesWordsRaw(findCommand(registry.all<Command>("command"), argv[lead])))
    usageExit(`${output[0]} before ${argv[lead]} is not read - ${argv[lead]} takes its words raw, with no output flags`);
mutations.expectRed: a leading output flag before a command that takes its words raw is a usage error, exit 1
mutations.cell: a leading output flag before a command that takes its words raw is a usage error, exit 1
mutations.note: The first B46 behavior: the move ran before the command was resolved.
